title: Saudi says Riyadh airport partly reopens despite renewed Houthi threats
gist: Reuters via Al-Monitor: Riyadh's King Khalid airport partly reopened Oct. 25 after a deadly Houthi attack, but Houthis threaten it again and daily missile/drone attacks continue, as the Yemen front shatters the 2022 truce and edges toward Bab el-Mandeb.

insights.claim: Saudi Arabia partially reopened two terminals of Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on Oct. 25, 2026 (Terminal 1 domestic, Terminal 2 international for national carriers), but Flightradar24 data showed little traffic.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Aviation and travel normalization in Riyadh is fragile.
insights.locator: Saudi Arabia said its main airport

insights.claim: The airport halted operations Oct. 10 after a Houthi-claimed attack killed 13 and wounded over 300, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade; the coalition counted 20 Houthi attacks on the airport between Oct. 1 and 11.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Sustained attacks raise Gulf operational and insurance risk.
insights.locator: The airport had halted operations on October 10

insights.claim: The Houthis continue daily attacks on Saudi Arabia, the world's largest oil exporter; they claimed strikes on the airport and Saudi oil facilities on Oct. 24, and Saudi Arabia intercepted 10 ballistic missiles fired toward the south.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Direct threat to Saudi oil infrastructure is an oil-price risk premium driver.

insights.claim: Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree renewed a warning that the Riyadh airport remains a military target and 'would never be safe'.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.quote: remained a "military target" and would "never be safe"

insights.claim: Saudi Arabia escalated strikes after the Houthis seized strategic Red Sea coastal territory last month, closing in on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a global chokepoint for Gulf oil shipments opposite Hormuz.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: A second chokepoint at risk alongside Hormuz; watch Red Sea shipping and crude flows.
insights.locator: Saudi Arabia has stepped up its strikes

insights.claim: The Yemen fighting has shattered a UN-brokered truce that had largely held since 2022 and has become a destabilizing element of the US-Israeli offensive against Iran, making Saudi Arabia a pressure point.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: The Iran war is widening to Gulf allies.
insights.locator: The conflict has become an increasingly destabilising element
